sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel (D), with 42 bipartisan co-sponsors
status: Passed House 201-1 on 2026-06-24; referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-25; reported as amended and re-referred to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-06-30.
key_provisions: Senate-amended PN 3727 would let a municipality adopt a public-meeting resolution pausing acceptance of new data-center land-development applications for up to 180 days, retroactive to specified public notice. Earlier applications are exempt and continue under the applicable earlier rules; submissions during a pause are deemed received the following day after it ends. Repeat use is barred for 18 months following formal expiration or repeal. This is optional local authority, not a statewide pause.

status: Legacy precursor memo linked by its official page to SB 1359, whose history lists referral to Senate Local Government on 2026-06-04. The separate claim about SB 1359 language offered as an amendment to another bill is not direct passage or failure of this bill and remains unverified here.
key_provisions: Pre-introduction memo proposing a three-year statewide hyperscale-data-center development moratorium, including described supporting infrastructure. The official page links to SB 1359, separately retained as pa-sb1359. This precursor proposal is not an additional independent bill or enacted statewide moratorium.

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel; Rep. Kyle Donahue; Rep. Kyle Mullins; Rep. Chris Pielli
status: Legacy precursor memo linked by the official memo page to HB 2496. The associated bill passed the House on 2026-06-24 and was reported amended with first consideration in the Senate on 2026-06-30. These are the bill's procedural events, not a second passage of the memo.
key_provisions: Pre-introduction memo proposing time for municipalities to develop data-center zoning rules; its official page links to HB 2496. The associated bill, separately retained as pa-hb2496, now contains the PN 3727 optional new-application pause with duration, earlier-application and repeat-use limits. This precursor row is not an additional independent bill.

sponsors: Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R), with Sens. Gebhard, Dush, Pennycuick, Bartolotta (R)
status: Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; reported as committed 10-1 on 2026-06-30; re-reported as amended (PN 1889) by Senate Rules and Executive Nominations 2026-07-11; second consideration in the Senate 2026-07-12. The later official history records re-referral to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations on 2026-09-30. Earlier vote particulars have not been independently revalidated here.
key_provisions: Re-reported PN 1889 proposes optional municipal resolutions temporarily pausing acceptance and consideration of specified new high-impact-data-center applications for up to 18 months, retroactive to the required public notice. It requires planning findings and hearing notice, preserves listed unrelated/maintenance activities, and exempts previously approved matters and qualifying pre-existing power-generation-site agreements. It does not itself enact a statewide or local moratorium.

sponsors: Sen. Katie Muth (D), with Sens. Comitta, Brown, Saval
party: D (prime sponsor); bipartisan co-sponsors including Sen. Rosemary Brown (R)
status: Retained official history lists referral to Senate Local Government on 2026-06-04. The prior record reports a 2-9 vote on proposed SB 1359 language offered to SB 1345; that related amendment is not a direct vote disposing of SB 1359. Its vote and procedural details remain unverified here.
key_provisions: Imposes a statewide moratorium on hyperscale data center development and permitting, with enforcement provisions; described in press coverage as a three-year moratorium. Appears to correspond to the 'Proposed statewide moratorium' co-sponsorship memo (#48102).

status: Amended in Senate Communications and Technology Committee (10-0, Amendment A02384, PN 1424) 2026-02-04; no further action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Creates Office of Transformation and Opportunity and AI/Data Center/Emerging Technology Regulatory Sandbox Program, including high-impact data center permits for facilities with their own power.

status: Referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2025-09-05; no further action through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Creates accelerated data center siting and DEP permitting process, including candidate sites and agency coordination.

status: Presented, ordered printed and referred to House Rules 2026-01-23; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-02; Continued to 2027 in Rules Committee (Voice Vote) 2026-02-06.
key_provisions: Introduced summary describes a temporary local approval pause until the earlier of fulfillment of all pending data-center-customer requests for interconnection to electric utility distribution service or 2028-07-01. The introduced bill and its full exceptions were not retained in the inspected attempts.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-06; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended laying on the table (9-Y 0-N) 2026-02-10; left in Labor and Commerce 2026-02-18; official retained page labels the bill failed.
key_provisions: Would require State Corporation Commission certificates of operation for new high-load facilities exceeding 25 MW, including review of grid sufficiency and customer cross-subsidy risks. The introduced eligibility condition concerns facilities not operating before 2026-07-01; that proposed applicability date is not an enacted effective date.

status: Passed House 2025-01-23 (57-Y 40-N); passed Senate with substitute 2025-02-12; conference report agreed to by Senate 2025-02-21 and House 2025-02-22; enrolled 2025-03-07; House rejected Governor's recommended amendments 2025-04-02 (11-Y 85-N); vetoed by Governor 2025-05-02. Subsequent veto proceedings were not independently established.
key_provisions: As-passed summary describes a proposal requiring a high energy use facility site assessment before rezoning, special exception, or special use permit approval, including sound effects on residential units and schools within 500 feet of the property boundary and optional review of water, agriculture, parks, historic sites and forestland. It also describes an existing-approval expansion/modification exception subject to qualified additional-power wording and preserves local zoning authority. The exact exception boundary and enrolled text remain unverified; enrolled text was not retained in the inspected attempts.

status: Passed House 2024-02-13 (55-Y 42-N 1-A); Senate continued the bill to 2025 in General Laws and Technology (9-Y 3-N 3-A) 2024-02-28; left in General Laws and Technology 2024-11-19. The retained official page labels the bill failed; complete 2025 proceedings were not independently established.
key_provisions: Would allow local site assessments before data center siting approvals; House-passed version focused on water use and carbon emissions.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-12; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-10; Continued to 2027 in Labor and Commerce (Voice Vote) 2026-02-12.
key_provisions: Would prevent utility costs substantially related to serving data center customers of 100 MW or more from being recovered from non-data-center customers unless rates substantially recover those costs from data centers. The introduced cost condition also requires that the relevant costs would not have been incurred but for that data-center demand.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-12; referred to House Counties, Cities and Towns; subcommittee recommended incorporating (Voice Vote) 2026-01-22; Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns into HB153 (Thomas) (Voice Vote) 2026-01-23.
key_provisions: Introduced proposal addressing specified localities' data-center zoning, including industrial designation, residential impacts and mitigation measures; incorporated into HB 153. Incorporation does not establish enactment of every introduced HB 511 provision.

status: Prefiled 2026-01-06; reported from Senate Local Government (15-Y 0-N) 2026-01-19; Incorporated by Finance and Appropriations into SB94 (Roem) (13-Y 2-N) 2026-02-03.
key_provisions: Related site-assessment bill incorporated into the enacted SB94 framework.

status: Passed Senate 2025-01-30 (33-Y 6-N 1-A); passed House with substitute 2025-02-12 (58-Y 39-N); conference report agreed to 2025-02-22; enrolled 2025-03-07; Senate rejected Governor's recommended amendments 2025-04-02 (16-Y 24-N); Vetoed by Governor 2025-05-02 (veto sustained; no override vote recorded).

Incorporates SB130 (Ebbin) 2026-02-03; passed Senate 2026-02-12 (21-Y 18-N 1-A); passed House with substitute 2026-02-25 (80-Y 14-N); conference report agreed to 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 568, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2026-07-01.
key_provisions: Published chapter/code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The chapter labels the provision 15.2-2209.4; the observed code publishes it as 15.2-2209.5. Later force is not independently confirmed.
